First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $3.$ We must make sure that *all* of the terms on the right-hand side are multiplied by $3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2n+6}{3} & =4n+1 \\ 3\cdot (\frac{2n+6}{3}) & =3\cdot (4n+1) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{2n+6}{\cancel{3}}) & =3\cdot 4n+3\cdot 1 \\ 2n+6 & =12n+3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2n+6 & =12n+3 \\ 2n+6-2n & =12n+3-2n \\ 6 & =10n+3 \\ 6-3 & =10n+3-3 \\ 3 & =10n \\ \frac{3}{10} & =\frac{10n}{10} \\ \frac{3}{10} & =n\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $n = \dfrac{3}{10}.$
